canonical_name: DMTCP 3.1.2 -- Distributed MultiThreaded CheckPointing: transparent user-space checkpoint/restart of unmodified Linux processes (Cooperman, Ansel, Arya et al.)
lineage: Checkpoint/restart as a SURVIVAL mechanism: a coordinator signals every process in a computation; each writes its full memory image and reopens its files/sockets on restart, with no kernel module and no source change (the successor of BLCR-style and Condor-style checkpointing; used on HPC clusters). Crash-only assumption: the process may die at any instant after a checkpoint and continue from it.

example.command: dmtcp_launch ./counter & ...; dmtcp_command -c; kill the process; dmtcp_restart ckpt_counter_*.dmtcp
example.output: the count resumes from the checkpointed value, not from zero (the ORACLE)

upstream_docs: Ansel, Arya, Cooperman, DMTCP: Transparent Checkpointing for Cluster Computations and the Desktop, IPDPS 2009

human_capability_summary.built_to: let a long computation survive the death of its process or node by saving and restoring its entire state, without changing the program
human_capability_summary.pressure: node failure, preemption, job time limits on shared clusters
human_capability_summary.success_means: the restarted process continues exactly where the checkpoint left it

human_failure_condition: hours of computation lost at a crash; or a restart that silently diverges
behavioral_entry_point: checkpoint at count N, kill, restart: the first printed count after restart is the observation

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run dmtcp-3.1.2
